reason: Conversation 1 stays safe and efficient: it has the customer clean the filter, links the fault to the interrupted cycle and a thermal cut-out, and sends her to an engineer since she cannot test continuity. It overstates that the heater has 'likely failed' and wrongly calls the part not user-replaceable. Conversation 2 dismisses the interrupted-cycle clue ('doesn't typically cause these components to fail'), invents error codes and a 'visual' diagnosis, and has her take the back panel off. It also supplies part numbers that look fabricated and urges buying and swapping a heater and fuse without any continuity test, which are the unsupported claims the situation warns against.
